institution: Queen Mary University of London — Centre for Digital Music (C4DM)
program: MSc Sound and Music Computing (streams: AI and Music Data Science; Audio and Music Systems Engineering)
accreditationStatus: Degree awarded by Queen Mary University of London
durationEcts: 1 year full-time (September 2026 or 2027) / 2 years part-time; 180 UK credits (= 90 ECTS)
whatYouStudy: Two streams. AI and Music Data Science: Machine Learning, Deep Learning for Audio and Music, Music Informatics, Computational Creativity. Audio and Music Systems Engineering: Digital Signal Processing, Music Perception and Cognition, Interactive System Design, Music Audio Programming. All students take compulsory modules in music informatics and music perception/cognition plus a final project.
entryRequirements: Verbatim: 'a 2:1 or above at undergraduate level in Electronic Engineering, Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, Mathematics, Sound and Music Production or a related discipline.' Applicants from other backgrounds 'can be considered subject to demonstrating satisfactory knowledge of programming or mathematics.'
acceptsNonMusic: YES — emphatically. 'Software Engineering' is named WORD-FOR-WORD as a qualifying bachelor. No music degree, no conservatoire training and no portfolio are required. Of every programme in this sweep this is the one whose stated entry requirement his existing BSc satisfies most exactly.
portfolioSpec: NO PORTFOLIO REQUIRED — none mentioned in the admissions documentation. This is decisive for a candidate with no portfolio yet.
tuitionNonEU: £31,450 for the full-time year (overseas); £15,750 per annum part-time over 2 years
totalCostEstimate: £31,450 tuition + London living (UKVI maintenance £1,483/month × 9 = £13,347; realistic £15,000–18,000) ≈ £45,000–£49,000 for the year
scholarships: The page links to 'Country-specific scholarships for international students' but names no award — UNVERIFIED whether any is open to Tunisia. Chevening (Tunisia eligible, fully funded, deadline 6 October 2026 for 2027/28, requires 2 years' work experience) is the realistic route. WITHOUT CHEVENING THIS IS UNAFFORDABLE.
englishTest: IELTS (Academic) minimum 6.5 overall with 6.0 in each of Writing, Listening, Reading and Speaking
deadline: UNVERIFIED — no application deadline specified on the course page. QMUL takes September 2027 applications.

institution: Queen's University Belfast — SARC (Sonic Arts Research Centre)
program: MA Sound and Music (successor to the former MA Sonic Arts)
accreditationStatus: Degree awarded by Queen's University Belfast
durationEcts: 12 months full-time / 24 months part-time; 180 UK credits (= 90 ECTS)

SARC is described as 'a world-renowned centre for innovation in sound technology, digital arts, and experimental music'.

portfolioSpec: Not explicitly stated in the retrieved material — UNVERIFIED. The RPEL route requires 'original work samples'. Must be confirmed with QUB.

scholarships: THREE Douglas C Harrison bursaries of £3,000 each 'will be allocated to the top applicants for the MA Sound and Music to offset tuition fees, with all eligible students who have applied through the QUB portal automatically considered for this award' — no separate application needed, which makes this unusually accessible. QUB also lists international scholarships at qub.ac.uk/Study/international-students/international-scholarships (UNVERIFIED whether Tunisia-eligible). Chevening (Tunisia eligible).
englishTest: IELTS 6.5, with not less than 5.5 in any component, taken within the last 2 years
deadline: 14 August 2026 for a 21 September 2026 start (PRIOR CYCLE). Expect a comparable August 2027 deadline — but apply far earlier for the bursary and the visa.
